metadata.title: Tech investors are fleeing to CrowdStrike—ignoring a 5,552x P/E

content.text:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Investing.com — AI chip and software leaders have been hammered in November. The abrupt resignation of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) chief executive Jensen Huang set off a technology sell-off on November 12. Yet investors fleeing that volatility have piled into cybersecurity as a safe haven, pushing CrowdStrike Holdings (NASDAQ:CRWD)—the AI-powered endpoint security leader—up 7.4% this week to $243.46 and Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) up 12.3% to $361.73.
Cybersecurity may feel like shelter from the AI sell-off, but buyers chasing CrowdStrike's green screen are paying a price that assumes nothing goes wrong. CrowdStrike trades at 5,552 times trailing earnings and Palo Alto Networks at 653 times, and InvestingPro's valuation models flag CrowdStrike as "Overvalued" at $127.28, 47.7% below the share price, with Palo Alto Networks also "Overvalued" at $236.90, 34.5% below its own. Revenue growth has accelerated for five straight quarters, but GAAP earnings have only just turned positive, so those multiples rest on growth alone.
Telling a genuine safe haven from a crowded trade is what ProPicks AI is built for. In Tech Titans, InvestingPro's strategy dedicated to high-margin tech leaders, neither cybersecurity name made the November lineup: the strategy would not pay 600x to 5,500x earnings for safety, and holds profitable cloud-security and chip-equipment leaders instead.
CrowdStrike makes its money selling subscriptions to its Falcon platform, and a single lightweight sensor is its pricing power: every new module—cloud, identity, next-gen SIEM, and now AI security—runs on the agent customers have already installed. That design is turning existing customers into bigger ones. Some 51% of subscription customers now use six or more modules, Falcon Flex annual recurring revenue (ARR) surpassed $2.29 billion with 101% year-over-year growth, and customers converting to Flex see ARR uplift of 40% or more.
Second-quarter fiscal 2027 results proved that AI is accelerating demand across the platform. Revenue climbed 26% year-over-year to $1.47 billion, the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration, and record net new ARR of $333 million surged 51%, topping the high end of guidance by more than $45 million. AI Detection and Response ARR nearly tripled from the first quarter, and next-gen SIEM ARR topped $695 million with roughly 60% growth.
The cash is following. Free cash flow hit a record $377 million, or 26% of revenue, and CrowdStrike holds $5.01 billion in cash. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance to revenue of $5.991 billion to $6.011 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.25 to $1.26, with a free cash flow margin of at least 30%.
The Street Says Buy, Fair Value Says Half Price
Most of the Street still rates CrowdStrike a Buy. Rosenblatt holds a Buy at $275, Deutsche Bank at $300, DA Davidson at $245 and Jefferies at $240, while Bernstein SocGen Group holds at $177. The median price target of $249.68 sits just above the current share price, with targets ranging from $132 to $325.
InvestingPro's Fair Value models take a far harder line, placing intrinsic value at $127.28 per share—47.7% below the share price and roughly half the Street's median target.
The GAAP numbers tell a thinner story. Over the last twelve months CrowdStrike posted a GAAP operating loss of $133.2 million, and second-quarter GAAP net income came to just $5.3 million, even as non-GAAP operating income hit a record $372 million. The stock trades at more than 190 times fiscal 2027 earnings forecasts, and InvestingPro gives it a profitability rating of only 3 out of 10. Third-quarter guidance implies revenue growth of 23% to 24%, a slowdown from 26%, and competition from Microsoft's bundled Defender offerings and Palo Alto Networks' platform expansion keeps pricing under pressure.
Timing adds to the risk. Chief executive George Kurtz sold $4.45 million of shares on November 6 and November 9 under a prearranged 10b5-1 trading plan. Third-quarter results are due on December 1, and at these multiples any sign of slower growth could hit the shares hard.
Before hiding out in cybersecurity after this week's surge, investors must weigh CrowdStrike's record ARR growth against a valuation that leaves no room for a miss. GAAP operating margins, stock-based compensation dilution, and federal spending exposure are detailed inside the CrowdStrike Holdings Pro Research Report.
CrowdStrike is winning the AI security build-out, with a platform that is still gaining speed. At today's multiple, though, investors piling in for safety are buying a stock that needs flawless execution simply to hold its ground.
Relying on a single cybersecurity stock while tech volatility drives money into crowded safe havens leaves capital exposed to the multiple compression that hits the most expensive names first. Rather than attempting to judge manually how much growth a quadruple-digit P/E can absorb, InvestingPro's data-driven strategies evaluate thousands of balance sheets every month to isolate tech leaders whose GAAP profits already justify their price.
